text:
opsbot: [INCIDENT ALERT] INC-2026-472: rapid autoscale churn -> node flaps detected in inference-prod (us-west-2). 5xx rate spike 18% -> 40% over last 6m. Top symptom: multiple pods crashlooping with OOMKilled / cuda errors. paging oncall.

mia: i’m live on this. seeing repeated `OOMKilled` + `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in runtime logs. cluster autoscaler is rapidly adding/removing nodes; pods bounce. allocating fresh gpu nodes then pod fails during init -> crashloop.

leo: can you paste the pod logs? suspecting model kv cache memory regen causing huge allocations on startup.

mia: logs below (trimmed):
```
2026-03-15T02:20:31Z inference-runtime: allocating kv cache size=24GB
2026-03-15T02:20:31Z runtime: cudaMalloc failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
2026-03-15T02:20:31Z container: TaskState: OOMKilled
2026-03-15T02:20:32Z kubelet: Restarting container with backoff
```

anya: hmm. that's similar to previous memory spiral. autoscaler keeps scaling because pods are Pending when node full -> then node removed since low utilization -> then many pods rescheduled -> repeat. we need to stop the feedback loop.

jamie: immediate mitigation: disable autoscaler for the affected nodepool, cordon new nodes? Or set a larger min for nodepool to prevent thrash.

sam: agreed. also need to reduce memory footprint on pod startup. can we pin to smaller model variant or enable kv cache warmup off? we can flip runtime env `KV_CACHE_INIT=false` as a hotfix.

mia: trying quick ingress: marking affected nodepool `gpu-autoscale-usw2` as `--min-size=3 --max-size=6` and pausing cluster-autoscaler. running:
```
gcloud container clusters update inference-prod --node-pool gpu-autoscale-usw2 --min-nodes 3 --max-nodes 6
kubectl annotate nodepool gpu-autoscale-usw2 autoscaler.paused=true --overwrite
```

devops-bot: cluster-autoscaler paused on nodepool/gpu-autoscale-usw2 (requested by mia). :white_check_mark:

leo: good. next, cordon nodes that are flapping to avoid new pods landing on them:
```
kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-autoscale-usw2 -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
```

anya: also we should rollout a temporary deployment patch to reduce replica burst and add startup probe to delay traffic until KV cache ready. patching now: `kubectl patch deployment inference-runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"KV_CACHE_INIT","value":"false"}],"livenessProbe":{"initialDelaySeconds":60}}]}}}}'`

jamie: i’ll push the patch to canary first (2 pods) and monitor errors.

taylor-cs: any customer impact? we’ve got a support ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about 502s starting ~02:18 UTC.

mia: last 10m: AcmeCorp 95th latency 22s, 50% error rate on generation route. marking SEV3 for now, might escalate to SEV2 if not resolved.

sam: monitoring metrics: pod restarts spiking at 02:16 -> 02:22. node flaps at 02:18 -> 02:24 (kube events show node NotReady then gone). Likely provider-side preemptions + autoscaler reacting.

leo: thought: provider preemptions could be the initial cause. But cudaIllegalAddress points to driver/kernel mismatch after node comes up with different CUDA minor version. any kernel driver upgrades in recent node image rollout?

devops-bot: recent node image release across region us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T22:00Z rolling: containerd v1.6.18, nvidia-driver 525.85.05 -> 525.85.05 (no version change). no auto-updates scheduled.

mia: ruled out node image delta for now. crash occurs before heavy inference, during KV cache alloc which is deterministic by model size. i suspect startup concurrency spike: all pods try to prime cache simultaneously when nodes scale up.

anya: mitigation 2: apply podAntiAffinity to spread startup across nodes and add `startupProbe` with backoff, and reduce replica surge. but that’s a medium-term change.

jamie: can we temporarily set HPA maxReplicas lower and enable burst queue so new load queues instead of instant replicas? patching HPA to max 20->8 now.

sam: applied HPA caps: inference-runtime-hpa.maxReplicas=8 (was 20). note: this may increase request latency but avoids crashstorms.

taylor-cs: updated AcmeCorp that we're mitigating; asked for any ongoing failures on their side - they confirm degraded but stable now.

mia: after pausing autoscaler + hpa cap + kvcache off, restarts dropped to near-zero, error rate down to ~6% in last 5m. keeping these while we stabilize.

leo: next steps: 1) add startup probe + staggered launch, 2) improve runtime to fail gracefully on cuda allocation with fallback to CPU or smaller kv cache, 3) autoscaler policy tweak to use `scaleDownDelay` and `buffered` thresholds to avoid reacting to transient Pending state.

any a: i'll open a follow-up ticket for autoscaler policy changes and long-term runtime work. recommend postmortem with timeline + customer impact. also create runbook entry for "autoscale thrash -> cuda OOM".

jamie: will revert canary to stable model variant after tests. also saving logs and adding `OOMKilled` grep for the incident page.

devops-bot: Note: paused autoscaler will auto-resume in 6h if not unpaused (safety). manual unpause recommended after review.

mia: thanks everyone. handing off to leo for next 2 hours as follow-up owner. leo, please take the oncall baton.

leo: taking it. will coordinate postmortem and liaise with support for customer updates. sending summary now.

text summary (leo): short summary posted to #incidents and epic ticket created INC-2026-472-PR. Root cause: startup concurrency during autoscale combined with runtime memory allocation behavior leading to CUDA allocation failure; contributing: aggressive autoscaler config and insufficient startup probes. Impact: several large customers (AcmeCorp, BetaAnalytics) experienced ~50% error rate for 12 minutes. Mitigations: paused autoscaler for gpu-autoscale-usw2, capped HPA, disabled KV_CACHE_INIT, cordoned flapping nodes. Action items: runtime fallback on alloc fail, modify autoscaler policy, add startup/staggering, postmortem.

sam: adding a note to infra: consider adding node warm pool for GPUs to avoid mass concurrent cold starts.

taylor-cs: I'll send customer follow-up template. tagging support-leads.

mia: leaving logs and commands in incident thread. marking as handoff -> oncall leo. :pushpin:
